rounds.text: Current Infraprojects Ltd is severely under-appreciated by the market, trading at a modest P/E of 12.7x despite delivering exceptional profitability metrics [E1, E9]. The company boasts a stellar return on equity and return on capital employed of 27.2% each, vastly outperforming sector median benchmarks of roughly 10% to 14% [E9, E10, E13, E49]. This fundamental strength translates into powerful top and bottom-line expansion, led by a compounded trailing twelve-month sales growth of 76% and profit growth of 49% [E14, E15]. Furthermore, capital expenditure is largely complete with capital-work-in-progress dropping to zero, signaling that new capacity is primed to come online [E27]. A discounted cash flow model reveals a substantial margin of safety of 44.0% with an intrinsic value of Rs 166 per share against a market price of Rs 93, while a reverse DCF indicates the current price prices in a meager 1.9% earnings growth [E32, E33, E34]. Conceded: [E16, E20, E22]

Despite reported profitability, Current Infraprojects Ltd exhibits severe cash generation failures that undermine the reported earnings quality [E20]. Operating cash flow for March 2026 sits deeply negative at Rs -9 Cr, translating to a catastrophic cash conversion of -0.64x against reported profit, with free cash flow plummeting to an alarming Rs -30 Cr [E20, E22]. This disconnect between accounting profits and actual cash realization coincides with an inconsistent operating-margin trend across both yearly and quarterly horizons [E18, E19]. Furthermore, the company offers a zero dividend yield despite reporting profits, withholding cash from shareholders while burning capital [E4, E38]. Institutional confidence is waning visibly, marked by a net negative institutional money flow and a reduction in foreign institutional holdings from 7.32% to 3.98% over two quarters [E29, E31]. Conceded: the company boasts high return metrics including an ROE of 27.2% and a strong trailing twelve-month sales growth of 76% [E13, E14]. However, the stock price has suffered a 39% decline over the past year, resting precariously at just 27% of its 52-week range while trading at premium valuation multiples compared to sector benchmarks, including an EV/EBITDA of 10.71x and a price-to-book ratio of 2.96x [E5, E7, E11, E16].

Conceded: operating cash flow was negative at Rs -9 Cr in Mar 2026 and free cash flow dropped to Rs -30 Cr [E20, E22]. However, the business is scaling aggressively with a compounded sales growth of 76% and profit growth of 49% over the trailing twelve months, demonstrating robust top-line momentum [E14, E15]. The capital expenditure cycle is largely complete as evidenced by CWIP falling 100% to Rs 0 Cr, indicating new capacity coming online to support future earnings [E27]. The current share price of Rs 93 sits significantly below the DCF intrinsic value of Rs 166 per share, offering a substantial 44.0% margin of safety [E2, E32, E33]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the market price only prices in a modest 1.9% earnings growth compared to the 10.0% base case, meaning expectations are heavily discounted [E34]. Conceded: the stock has declined 39% over the past year and trades at a higher EV/EBITDA of 10.71x versus the sector benchmark of 8.63x [E11, E16]. Yet, domestic institutions have actually increased their stake from 9.69% to 10.67% by Mar 2026, and stellar return metrics including an ROCE of 25.74% against a sector benchmark of 12.39% easily justify the premium valuation [E10, E30].

Conceded: domestic institutions increased their stake to 10.67% [E30], and ROCE reaches 25.74% against a sector benchmark of 12.39% [E10]. However, total institutional money flow reads NEGATIVE MONEY FLOW with an aggregate holding change of -2.36 percentage points, driven by foreign institutions slashing their stake from 7.32% to 3.98% [E29, E31]. While the bull highlights aggressive sales growth of 76% and profit growth of 49% [E14, E15], this top-line expansion has coincided with a complete breakdown in cash generation, producing an operating cash flow of negative Rs -9 Cr and free cash flow of negative Rs -30 Cr in Mar 2026 [E20, E22]. The claim that a completed capex cycle [E27] justifies a 44% margin of safety from a DCF model [E33] ignores the reality that the stock price has plunged 39% over the past year [E16] and sits at just 27% of its 52-week range [E5], reflecting deep market skepticism toward these reported profits. Furthermore, the EV/EBITDA multiple of 10.71x trades at a sharp premium to the sector benchmark of 8.63x [E11], and the company pays a dividend yield of 0.00% while offering inconsistent operating margins over the last three quarters [E4, E19].
